body:
> @aloubyansky the showcase in this case does not actually reference a parent pom. Should we actually do workspace discovery in this case?

Yes, there was a request recently to enable this kind of discovery as this what IDEs do and what users expect apparently.

One of the issue is that, this kind of project may (and most probably will be) referenced as a module. So it is built as part of the whole workspace. So `compile` and `test` will include it and make it available on the classpath even if it's not installed in the local repo. And this is what we should do as well for the dev mode.

I dont understand why the classes got a different classloader at all. The direct depenendcies of the showcase are:
myfaces-quarkus-deployment
myfaces-quarkus-runtime
primefaces

myfaces-quarkus-deployment has the dependency to myfaces-api and myfaces-impl.

so why myfaces-api and primefaces has a different classloader? they are both in the same scope actually, both are required compile and runtime dependencies

Guys, have tested with master (commit 85a79411e3a63e9f931bc43e12fbcce1215df676) and dev mode works as expected.

The only issue I had was with test classpath:
1 - I had to add 
```
 <dependency> 
            <groupId>com.fasterxml.woodstox</groupId>
            <artifactId>woodstox-core</artifactId>
            <version>5.0.2</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
```

Otherwise I get `Caused by: javax.xml.stream.FactoryConfigurationError: Provider com.ctc.wstx.stax.WstxInputFactory not found`

2 - I had to add 
```
<dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.httpcomponents</groupId>
            <artifactId>httpmime</artifactId>
            <version>4.5.12</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
```

Otherwise I get `ClassNotFoundException: org.apache.http.entity.mime.content.ContentBody`

Is this expected? I didn't needed those additional deps in v1.2.1.

@rmpestano can you update your reproducer in a state that is not working (and your added dependencies commented out)?

/cc @stuartwdouglas could it be related to your fix? Looks like it could be.

It should not be related to my fix, my fix should just remove some modules from the hot deployment capable list, it should not affect transitive dependencies. 

To figure out why this is happening I would need full stack traces of both so I can see what is actually using these.
